create.name: Centro Zen Anshin
create.bio:
Centro Zen Anshin is a Soto Zen practice centre in Rome's Trastevere district, a couple of minutes' walk from Trastevere station. It is led by Guglielmo Doryu Cappelli and Annamaria Gyoetsu Epifania, both Dharma heirs of Shohaku Okumura, so the centre belongs to the Sanshin line of Soto Zen; Doryu is authorised by the Soto school to teach outside Japan and is active in interfaith dialogue and in schools. Both teachers are also professional dancers and choreographers, and the centre's wider programme includes creative dance and tai chi. Its practice and facilities are open to everyone, whatever their faith or culture, and newcomers begin with an orientation talk and an introduction to the forms.

Zazen with morning service is held early on Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday, with evening sittings on Tuesday and a Friday evening of work practice, zazen and a Dharma talk; several sessions can also be joined online. Monthly ceremonies include the bodhisattva precepts renewal and a service for world peace, and there are regular sesshin, robe-sewing retreats and seasonal sesshin for the Buddha's birth, awakening and death. A monthly Saturday series introduces the basics of Buddhism for a free offering. Doryu's YouTube channel holds hundreds of Italian Dharma talks, including a long series on the Shodoka.

courses.title: Conoscere il Buddhismo – Incontri Mensili
courses.description: A monthly Saturday evening introduction to the basic principles of Buddhism with Doryu Cappelli, open to all with no prior knowledge, beginning with a welcome tea. Remaining dates run from 12 December 2026 to 5 June 2027.

courses.title: Pratica ad Anshin – orari della pratica
courses.description: The weekly timetable of zazen, walking meditation, morning and evening services and Friday Dharma talks, with monthly precepts and peace ceremonies; several sessions are also online. Beginners have an orientation talk first.

courses.title: Sesshin – ritiri mensili
courses.description: Monthly intensive practice retreats of one or more days, open to all, with zazen, ceremonies, work practice, formal oryoki meals and Dharma talks. Upcoming dates on the calendar include a Rohatsu sesshin on 4–6 December 2026.
